    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The opening names the cracked half-dry rods before explaining the equally half-dry group and

      renders being double-minded, without changing neither-living-nor-dead into a judgment that they

  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The working text has “have repented,” including the slower group; Michigan uses future repentance

      distinction and persistent-deeds warning are retained.'
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Be rivals” supplies the sense of the elliptical second phrase, which lacks a repeated jealousy
      noun in Athos and the working text. Michigan likely has the same omission; surrounding line ends
      are damaged, Bonner printed pp. 106–107. More literal alternative: “All these are foolish, having
      matters with one another over first place.” The first phrase explicitly has jealousy. “First place”
      can also mean precedence; no particular church office is named.'

    text: “Patience” renders makrothymia, also long-suffering or forbearance; humility renders tapeinophrosynē.

      keeping the commandments and retains the death warning for divisive and lawless people.

  text: '“Listen also about those who handed in half-dry rods with cracks. Those whose rods were equally

    2. “Those whose rods were half dry and cracked both waver and slander. They are never at peace with
    one another, but are always divided. Yet repentance is offered to these too. You see that some have
    repented, and they still have hope of repentance.”

    slowly will dwell in the walls. But those who do not repent and persist in their deeds will die.”[b]


    4. “Those who handed in green rods with cracks have always been faithful and good, but had some jealousy
    toward one another over first place and honor. All these are foolish to be rivals with one another
    over first place.”[c]


    5. “But these too heard my commandments. Being good, they cleansed themselves and quickly repented.
    Their dwelling came to be in the tower. But if anyone turns back to division, that person will be
    thrown out of the tower and lose their life.”


    6. “Life belongs to all who keep the Lord’s commandments. The commandments concern neither first place
    nor honor, but a person’s patience and humility. In such people is the Lord’s life; among those who
